The file system is only the fs parameter. Write no test file: a probe tests you and a judge writes the example tests. ## Function Cage Path A path the model wrote, admitted only when it names a listed file (or a directory of listed files) whose real path stays inside the root and outside .git. Behaviour: cagePath(tree {root, files: the listing, root-relative "/" paths}, path, kind "file" | "dir", fs {realpath, readFile}) → {ok true, path: the normalised relative path} | {ok false, error};

in a message is the path as given. In order: every "\" read as "/"; starting "/" or a drive /^[A-Za-z]:\// → "absolute path refused:

"; a segment ".." → "path leaves the root:

"; the segments without "" and "." → a segment ".git" → "inside .git:

"; rel = them "/"-joined; rel "" → dir: {ok, ""} (the root), file: "empty path". dir: some listed file starts with rel + "/" → {ok, rel}, else "no such directory in the tree:

" (directories are never resolved). file: rel not in the listing → "not in the tree (missing, ignored or a directory):

"; real = fs.realpath(posix join of root and rel), a throw → "no such file:

"; rootReal = fs.realpath(root); real must start with rootReal + "/", else "symlink out of the root refused:

" (a sibling sharing the root's prefix is outside); the rest of real after it holding a segment ".git" → "inside .git:

"; → {ok, rel}. readFile is never called. Ignored files are refused because the listing (git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard, read in P13b) does not hold them. Read docs/TASK_P13a_scout.md sections 2.2 (src/scout/parseTurn.ts, Parse Turn and its table) and 4. Write src/scout/parseTurn.ts, a NEW pure file of the layer scout that imports nothing. It exports, in this order, ScoutAction, ScoutAnswer, Turn, VERBS and parseTurn(text) exactly as section 2.2 shows: one action line per turn found by the verb regex on each line's trimStart (upper case only), READ's optional trailing range, GREP split at the last " -- " and its pattern compiled once to reject an invalid one, LIST's path, ANSWER's JSON from the first "{" to the last "}" checked key by key, every malformed reason exactly as pinned. Write no test file: a probe tests you and a judge writes the example tests.

## Function Parse Turn

One model turn of the scout protocol read as one action, one final answer or a malformed turn with its reason.

Behaviour: parseTurn(text: string | null) → Turn. VERBS = ["READ", "GREP", "LIST", "ANSWER"]. 1. null, or a text whose trim is "" → malformed "empty turn". 2. lines = text split on "\n", one trailing "\r" removed from each; an action line is a line whose trimStart matches /^(READ|GREP|LIST|ANSWER)(?=\s|$)/ (upper case only; prose and fence lines around it are ignored). None → malformed "no action: one line must start with READ, GREP, LIST or ANSWER"; more than one → malformed "<n> actions in one turn (<their verbs in order, ", "-joined>): send one per turn". 3. args = the action line trimmed, without its verb, trimmed. READ: args "" → "READ needs a path"; args matching /^(.*\S)\s+(\d+)-(\d+)$/ → path = group 1, from and to = Number of groups 2 and 3, from < 1 or to < from → "READ: bad line range <from>-<to>"; else path = args, from and to null. GREP: split args at its LAST " -- ": pattern = the part before, trimmed, path = the part after, trimmed; without " -- " the pattern is args and the path "". pattern "" → "GREP needs a pattern"; new RegExp(pattern) throws → "GREP: invalid pattern /<pattern>/". LIST: path = args ("" is the root). 4. ANSWER: rest = the action line (trimStart) after its verb, then every following line, "\n"-joined; the JSON is rest from its first "{" to its last "}" (no "{", or the last "}" before it → "ANSWER: no JSON object"); JSON.parse throws → "ANSWER: the JSON does not parse"; targets must be an array of non-empty strings with at least one ("ANSWER: targets must be a non-empty list of paths"); context_slice absent → [], else an array of non-empty strings ("ANSWER: context_slice must be a list of paths"); reasoning absent → "", else a string ("ANSWER: reasoning must be a string"); the answer carries only targets, context_slice, reasoning, in that order, the lists as given. Results: {kind "action", action: {kind "read", path, from, to} | {kind "grep", pattern, path} | {kind "list", path}}, {kind "answer", answer}, {kind "malformed", reason}; keys in these orders.

Steps:
- reads: Model Turn
- produces: Turn

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given "I will check the cage first.\nREAD src/scout/cagePath.ts"; "READ lib/b one.ts 12-40"; " READ src/a.ts 7-7\r\n"; when parseTurn; then actions read {path "src/scout/cagePath.ts", from null, to null}; {path "lib/b one.ts", from 12, to 40}; {path "src/a.ts", from 7, to 7}
2. given "GREP readOwnership|readMorphLog -- src/git"; "GREP a -- b -- tests"; "GREP export function"; when parseTurn; then actions grep {pattern "readOwnership|readMorphLog", path "src/git"}; {pattern "a -- b", path "tests"}; {pattern "export function", path ""}
3. given "LIST"; "```\nLIST tests/fixtures\n```"; when parseTurn; then actions list {path ""}; {path "tests/fixtures"}
4. given "Done.\nANSWER\n```json\n{\"targets\": [\"src/x.ts\"], \"reasoning\": \"GREP found it\", \"acceptance\": \"npm test\"}\n```"; then "ANSWER {\"context_slice\": [\"c.ts\"], \"reasoning\": \"r\", \"targets\": [\"a.ts\", \"b.ts\"]}"; when parseTurn; then answer {targets ["src/x.ts"], context_slice [], reasoning "GREP found it"} (acceptance dropped); answer {targets ["a.ts", "b.ts"], context_slice ["c.ts"], reasoning "r"}, JSON.stringify of the turn exactly {"kind":"answer","answer":{"targets":["a.ts","b.ts"],"context_slice":["c.ts"],"reasoning":"r"}}
5. given null; " \n\t"; "The change is in src/a.ts"; "Read src/a.ts"; "READX a"; "READ src/a.ts\nGREP x"; "READ"; "READ a.ts 9-3"; "READ a.ts 0-3"; "GREP ( -- src"; "GREP"; when parseTurn; then malformed "empty turn" twice; "no action: one line must start with READ, GREP, LIST or ANSWER" three times; "2 actions in one turn (READ, GREP): send one per turn"; "READ needs a path"; "READ: bad line range 9-3"; "READ: bad line range 0-3"; "GREP: invalid pattern /(/"; "GREP needs a pattern"
6. given "ANSWER the cage"; "ANSWER {targets: [a]}"; "ANSWER {\"targets\": []}"; "ANSWER {\"targets\": [\"a\", \"\"]}"; "ANSWER {\"targets\": [\"a\"], \"context_slice\": \"b\"}"; "ANSWER {\"targets\": [\"a\"], \"reasoning\": 5}"; when parseTurn; then malformed "ANSWER: no JSON object"; "ANSWER: the JSON does not parse"; "ANSWER: targets must be a non-empty list of paths" twice; "ANSWER: context_slice must be a list of paths"; "ANSWER: reasoning must be a string"

Data Model Turn: The text of one model answer (Answer.text of the processor), null when the provider gave none.
Schema:
string | null

Data Turn: What Parse Turn returns.
Schema:
{ kind: 'action', action: Scout Action } | { kind: 'answer', answer: { targets: string[], context_slice: string[], reasoning: string } } | { kind: 'malformed', reason: string }

## Function Seed From Ownership

The head of git's ownership as the scout's seed — the code the project's cards wrote, newest first — and its round-zero text.

Behaviour: seedFromOwnership(ownership {paths: {path, writes: {card, model, run}[]}[]} (git's Read Ownership result, most recently written first), files: the tree's listing, limit) → {source "primer", files, notes}. Walk the paths in order while fewer than limit are kept; keep a path in the listing whose language profileForPath is not null and that is not a test of that profile (language isTest: a test directory or the test file pattern). Its note: "<path>: written by " + its first SEED_WRITES (3) writes "<card> (<model or — when "">, run <run or —>)" "; "-joined, + "; … <k> more" when k more. SEED_FILES = 6, SEED_CHARS = 8000 (P13b's defaults). renderSeed(seed, maxChars) → "" when seed.files is empty; else SEED_HEADER ("Seed: code the project's cards wrote, most recently written first (git Morph-Card trailers):") + "\n", then each note as "- <note>\n" while the text stays ≤ maxChars chars; the first note that does not fit and every later one are left out and "- … <k> more seeded file|files not shown\n" is appended (past maxChars if need be). Pure: no file read.

Steps:
- uses: language
- reads: Seed Ownership
- produces: Scout Seed

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given ownership paths in order: tests/q.test.ts [q-judge m/r —], src/q.ts [q m/q 20261110-101010, q1 m/q R1, q0 "" null, qq m/x R0], docs/n.md, src/gone.ts, tools/x.py [x m/p R2], src/p.spec.ts, lib/c.ts [c m/c null], web/app.tsx [w m/w R3]; files = all but src/gone.ts; when seedFromOwnership(…, 3); then files ["src/q.ts", "tools/x.py", "lib/c.ts"]; notes "src/q.ts: written by q (m/q, run 20261110-101010); q1 (m/q, run R1); q0 (—, run —); … 1 more", "tools/x.py: written by x (m/p, run R2)", "lib/c.ts: written by c (m/c, run —)"
2. given the same; then {paths []}; when limit 10; limit 0; then limit 6; then files + "web/app.tsx" (note "web/app.tsx: written by w (m/w, run R3)"); files [] notes []; {source "primer", files [], notes []}
3. given the seed of example 1; when renderSeed with 8000; with the header + the first note line exactly; with 10; renderSeed of the empty seed; then SEED_HEADER + "\n" + the three "- <note>\n"; the header, the first note, "- … 2 more seeded files not shown\n"; the header, "- … 3 more seeded files not shown\n"; ""

Data Seed Ownership: The part of git's Ownership the seed reads (structurally Read Ownership's result).
Schema:
{ paths: { path, writes: { card, model, run: string | null }[] }[] }

Data Scout Seed: What Seed From Ownership returns.
Schema:
{ source: 'primer', files: string[], notes: string[] }

Read docs/TASK_P13a_scout.md sections 2.2 (src/scout/spendBudget.ts, Spend Budget and its table) and 4. Write src/scout/spendBudget.ts, a NEW pure file of the layer scout that imports nothing. It exports, in this order, ScoutBudgets, DEFAULT_BUDGETS, ScoutSpent, BudgetName, Charge, Charged, CLIP_MARKER, FINAL_TURN, spendTurn(budgets, spent, charge, elapsedMs) and stopReason(answered, closed, why) exactly as section 2.2 shows: the clip at the remaining characters with the marker counted, the new counts, the first closed budget in the order deadline, rounds, calls, reads, chars with its sentence, the input not changed. Write no test file: a probe tests you and a judge writes the example tests.

## Function Spend Budget

One turn charged against the five budgets; the first closed budget and its sentence; the stop_reason.

Behaviour: spendTurn(budgets {calls, reads, chars, rounds, deadlineMs}, spent {calls, reads, chars, rounds}, charge {call, read, text}, elapsedMs) → {spent, text, closed, why}; spent is not changed. remaining = budgets.chars − spent.chars; text = charge.text when its length ≤ remaining, else its first max(remaining, 0) chars + CLIP_MARKER ("\n[… clipped: the character budget is spent]"). The new spent: calls + 1 when call, reads + 1 when read, chars + the delivered text's length (the marker counted), rounds + 1 always (a malformed turn is charged call false, read false). closed = the first that holds, in this order: elapsedMs ≥ deadlineMs → "deadline", why "the deadline (<deadlineMs / 1000> s) passed"; rounds ≥ budgets.rounds → "rounds", "the round budget is spent (<rounds> of <budgets.rounds> rounds)"; calls → "the call budget is spent (<n> of <b> calls)"; reads → "the read budget is spent (<n> of <b> reads)"; chars → "the character budget is spent (<n> of <b> chars)" (each ≥, with the new counts); else null, null. FINAL_TURN = ["calls", "reads", "chars"]: after one of these closes the loop grants one answer-only turn; after deadline or rounds none. DEFAULT_BUDGETS = {calls 30, reads 12, chars 120000, rounds 40, deadlineMs 1800000}. stopReason(answered, closed, why): answered and closed null → "the model answered on its own"; answered → "the model answered after the budget closed: <why>"; closed → "no answer: <why>"; else "no answer: the session ended with every budget open". Keys in the orders written.

Steps:
- reads: Scout Budgets
- produces: Charged Turn

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given budgets B {calls 3, reads 2, chars 50, rounds 10, deadlineMs 60000}, spent 0 0 0 0, charge {call true, read true, text 20 × "x"}, elapsed 0; when spendTurn; then {spent {calls 1, reads 1, chars 20, rounds 1}, text the same, closed null, why null}
2. given B, spent {1, 1, 40, 1}, charge {call true, read false, text 25 × "y"}, elapsed 1000; when spendTurn; then {spent {2, 1, 93, 2}, text 10 × "y" + "\n[… clipped: the character budget is spent]", closed "chars", why "the character budget is spent (93 of 50 chars)"}
3. given B; spent {2, 0, 0, 2} + {call true, read false, "ok"}; spent {0, 1, 0, 0} + {true, true, ""}; spent {1, 0, 10, 9} + {false, false, "no action"}; when spendTurn at 0; then closed "calls" "the call budget is spent (3 of 3 calls)"; "reads" "the read budget is spent (2 of 2 reads)" (spent {1, 2, 0, 1}); "rounds" "the round budget is spent (10 of 10 rounds)" with spent {1, 0, 19, 10}
4. given spent {2, 1, 45, 9}, charge {true, true, 10 × "z"}; when spendTurn with B at 60000; B at 59999; B with rounds 40; also calls 30; also reads 12; B with deadlineMs 1500 at 1500; then "deadline" "the deadline (60 s) passed"; "rounds"; "calls"; "reads"; "chars" "the character budget is spent (93 of 50 chars)"; "deadline" "the deadline (1.5 s) passed"
5. given stopReason(true, null, null); (true, "reads", "the read budget is spent (2 of 2 reads)"); (false, "deadline", "the deadline (60 s) passed"); (false, null, null); when stopReason; then "the model answered on its own"; "the model answered after the budget closed: the read budget is spent (2 of 2 reads)"; "no answer: the deadline (60 s) passed"; "no answer: the session ended with every budget open"; FINAL_TURN ["calls", "reads", "chars"]; DEFAULT_BUDGETS as written

Data Scout Budgets: The five budgets and what one session has spent.
Schema:
budgets { calls, reads, chars, rounds, deadlineMs }; spent { calls, reads, chars, rounds }

Data Charged Turn: What Spend Budget's spendTurn returns.
Schema:
{ spent, text, closed: 'deadline'|'rounds'|'calls'|'reads'|'chars' | null, why: string | null }

## Function Run Tool

One READ, GREP or LIST executed over the listing through the cage and the injected file system, its text capped.

Behaviour: runTool(action, tree, fs, caps {readLines, grepHits, grepLineChars, listEntries, grepSkip: string[]}) → {text, read: action is a READ, error: string | null}. DEFAULT_TOOL_CAPS = {readLines 400, grepHits 200, grepLineChars 300, listEntries 300, grepSkip [".morph", "decks"]}. A failure: error = its message, text = "<READ|GREP|LIST> failed: <error>"; else error null and text = its lines "\n"-joined, no final newline. A file's lines: its text split on "\n", one trailing "\r" removed from each, the last piece dropped when it is "". The listing is walked in code-unit order. READ: Cage Path (file) refused → its error; fs.readFile(posix join of root and the caged path) throws → "unreadable: <path>"; a "\0" in it → "binary file: <path>"; 0 lines → the one line "READ <path>: empty file"; from = action.from ?? 1, from > n lines → "line range <from>-<action.to ?? n> is past the end (<n> lines): <path>"; to = min(action.to ?? n, n), last = min(to, from + readLines − 1): "READ <path> lines <from>-<last> of <n>", then "<i>: <line i>" for i from..last, then when last < to "… <to − last> more lines; READ <path> <last + 1>-<to> for the next". GREP: new RegExp(pattern) (no flags) throws → "invalid pattern /<pattern>/"; Cage Path (dir) refused → its error; skip = grepSkip, or none when the caged path's first segment is in grepSkip; each listed file under the caged path whose first segment is not skipped: Cage Path (file) refused or readFile throws → counted refused; a "\0" → passed over silently; each line i that the pattern tests true is a match, shown while fewer than grepHits are shown as "<file>:<i>: <line>", a line longer than grepLineChars as its first grepLineChars chars + "… (+<the rest's length> chars)". Lines: "GREP /<pattern>/ in <'the tree' or the caged path + '/'>: <m> match|matches in <f> file|files" (f = files with a match), the shown matches, "… <m − shown> more matches" when any left, "(<r> file|files refused by the cage)" when r > 0. LIST: Cage Path (dir) refused → its error; entries = the next segment of each listed file under the caged path: a file name, or a directory name + "/" with the count of its files; entries in code-unit order: "LIST <'.' or the caged path + '/'>: <k> entry|entries", the first listEntries as "<name>" or "<dir>/ (<c> file|files)", "… <k − listEntries> more entries" when more. LIST and GREP never read a directory; LIST reads no file.

Steps:
- calls: Cage Path
- reads: Scout Action

- produces: Tool Result
